whyMatters.en: Duck walk, double-stop riffs, cars and school halls: Chuck Berry writes Rock 'n' Roll's shared guitar dialect—later bands still speak it with accents.
whyMatters.zh: 鸭步、双音 riff、汽车与校园走廊：Chuck Berry 写出 Rock 'n' Roll 的通用吉他方言——后来的乐队都带着口音还在说。

note.zh: 乡村节奏遇上电吉他弯音

interviewQuotes.text: The guitar is the most important thing.
interviewQuotes.speaker: Chuck Berry

shortBio.en: The founding architect of Rock 'n' Roll guitar grammar.
shortBio.zh: Rock 'n' Roll 吉他语法的奠基人。

body.en:
Chuck Berry turns the electric guitar into a storytelling engine: teenage motion, chrome, and punchlines that land on the backbeat.

Almost every guitar band after him is still paying rent on that language.
body.zh:
Chuck Berry 把电吉他变成讲故事的引擎：少年动作、镀铬光泽、落在后拍上的包袱。

之后几乎所有吉他乐队，都还在付这门语言的租金。

body.en:
Berry does not invent electricity. He invents the sentence structure: intro riff as headline, verse as road movie, solo as victory lap.

When Lennon, Keith Richards, or a thousand garage kids open with that double-stop bounce, they are citing him—whether they admit it or not.
body.zh:
Berry 没有发明电。他发明了句子结构：前奏 riff 当标题，主歌当公路电影，solo 当胜利圈。

Lennon、Keith Richards，或一千个车库小孩一弹起那双音弹跳，就是在引用他——承认与否无关。

title.zh: Maybellene：乡村速度遇上电音弯音

body.en:
1955. A car chase in song form—country rhythm under electric sting. Maybellene makes motion itself the plot.

Rock 'n' Roll learns it can be about engines and desire without waiting for a ballad's permission.
body.zh:
1955 年。一首歌形状的飙车——乡村节奏托着电吉他的刺。Maybellene 让「移动」本身成为情节。

Rock 'n' Roll 学会：不必等情歌批准，也能写引擎与欲望。

title.en: Johnny B. Goode: the guitar-hero prototype
title.zh: Johnny B. Goode：吉他英雄原型

body.en:
A kid who can play a guitar like ringing a bell. Johnny B. Goode is autobiography dressed as myth—and the template for every later guitar-hero montage.

The riff is a name tag. Once you hear it, every arena solo owes a quiet tip of the hat.
body.zh:
一个能把吉他弹得像摇铃的孩子。Johnny B. Goode 是披着神话外衣的自传——也是后来所有吉他英雄蒙太奇的模板。

riff 像名牌。听过一次，之后每个体育馆 solo 都欠一个安静的脱帽礼。

title.zh: 大家还在说 Chuck 语

body.en:
From British Invasion covers to punk's three-chord sprint, Berry's dialect survives translation. The duck walk becomes posture; the riff becomes muscle memory.

On the genre map he is not a side note. He is the road the map is drawn on.
body.zh:
从 British Invasion 的翻唱到朋克的三和弦冲刺，Berry 的方言经得起翻译。鸭步变成姿态，riff 变成肌肉记忆。

在流派图上他不是注脚。他是地图下面那条路。

title.en: Cars, girls, and a ringing bell
title.zh: 汽车、女孩，与摇铃般的吉他

body.en:
Berry's own lines keep landing on concrete nouns—cars, school, the guitar as a bell. No fog, no thesis statement.

That concreteness is why the quotes still cut: Rock 'n' Roll begins as reportage with a backbeat.
body.zh:
Berry 自己的句子总落在具体名词上——汽车、学校、像铃一样的吉他。没有雾，没有论文提纲。

具体，所以金句仍锋利：Rock 'n' Roll 一开始就是带后拍的现场报道。

note.en: Duck-walk riffs made rock portable and teachable.
note.zh: 鸭步 riff 让摇滚变得可携带、可传授。
